title: rhus semialata var. roxburghii
intro: Rhus semialata var. roxburghii, commonly known as the Roxburgh's sumac, is a plant species belonging to the family Anacardiaceae. It is traditionally used in medicine for its numerous health benefits, which include treating fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions such as eczema and acne. The therapeutic actions of R. semialata var. roxburghii include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties, making it effective in reducing inflammation and promoting wound healing. The bioactive constituents of this plant include tannins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
